Subject: Synthex renewal: term & unit pricing realignment + order form

Hi Ravi —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Based on the usage trends you shared and your stated desire to lock in price protection through 2029, I pulled together a proposed restructured renewal: a 24‑month term (Jan 1, 2029 — Dec 31, 2030) with a blended unit price that gives you ~18% off the on‑demand rate once the committed units are met.

Attached is the draft order form (OrderForm_Synthex_v3.pdf) and the clean MSA with the small changes we discussed. Two asks to keep things moving:

- Can you confirm that the expanded capacity target is 1.5M generation tokens/month?
- Do you need any additional SOC2 artifacts for procurement?

Looping in Kim (legal) and Tessa (billing/procurement) to validate the redlines and sign‑path. If this looks directionally right I can push the redline and send a DocuSign packet by end of week.

Best,
Lauren

Subject: Re: Synthex renewal: term & unit pricing realignment + order form

Lauren —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side after running the numbers with finance:

1) Term: engineering prefers a 12‑month initial term with an automatic renewal option (to allow us to re‑benchmark performance in 12 months). Possible?
2) Capacity: the 1.5M tokens/month estimate is our target peak; for contracting we need a clear burst/overage mechanism and a committed baseline of 1.0M tokens/month.
3) Pricing: finance is comfortable with the blended price, but we'd like the first six months invoiced monthly, then quarterly thereafter (to match internal cashflow).

I've attached the procurement team's template (pricing_workbook.xlsx) and copied Natalie + contracts to route the MSA redline back to you. If you can incorporate the 12‑month term option and explicit overage formula we'll expedite on our side.

—Ravi

Date: Wed, 12 Sep 2028 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Synthex renewal: term & unit pricing realignment + order form

Ravi —

Thanks — clear asks. Kim/Tessa: can you review the two commercial asks (12‑month initial term with auto‑renew; committed baseline 1.0M + burst rules) and the invoicing cadence change? Below are the target edits I propose before we send a redline:

- Term: 12 months initial, with an optional auto‑renew for 12 months unless either party provides 60 days' notice. (This preserves Synthex's re‑benchmark window while giving Redwood cadence.)
- Commit vs Burst: Commit = 1.0M tokens/month; Burst allowed up to 1.5M/month at 1.25x committed unit price for overage tokens.
- Invoicing: first 6 months invoiced monthly, thereafter quarterly in arrears.
- SLA credits: keep existing credit algorithm but cap total credits at 10% of monthly invoice. Kim — is that acceptable?

If legal confirms I'll circulate a redline of the MSA and an annotated order form ready for DocuSign.

Lauren

Date: Thu, 13 Sep 2028 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Synthex renewal: term & unit pricing realignment + order form

Lauren/Tessa —

I reviewed the proposed commercial edits and drafted redline notes for the MSA. Major points below (detailed comments in Synthex_MSA_redline.docx):

1) Term & auto‑renew: Acceptable with one tweak — change notice window to 90 days for contract stability on our forecasting side.

2) Commit/Burst language: Need explicit definition of what counts as a "token" for billing (generation tokens vs. prompt+generation). Recommend: bill on generation tokens only and include an example table in the order form.

3) Overage multiplier: 1.25x looks fine, but add a minimum overage bucket of 10k tokens to avoid micro‑bills.

4) SLA credits cap: 10% monthly cap is fine; however, we should carve out availability incidents caused by third‑party cloud outages (force majeure carveout).

5) Data retention & audit logs: Procurement asked for 3 years retention for audit logs (they prefer 7). We can offer 3 years standard and a paid add‑on for 7 years — call out in Exhibit B.

6) Invoicing cadence: Acceptable but we need to confirm billing contact and PO workflow for DocuSign routing. Tessa, can you confirm who signs and whether they use PO # on invoices?

I'll attach the redline. Once they confirm the token definition and notice window I'll prepare the DocuSign packet.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: Synthex_MSA_redline.docx

Kim, Lauren —

Thanks for the quick review. A few confirmations from procurement/finance: 

- We can accept the token definition as generation tokens only. Please include a sample calculation row in the order form.
- 90 days' notice for auto‑renew is acceptable.
- 1.25x overage multiplier and 10k token floor OK.
- Audit log retention: we'll accept 3 years for now, but request the add‑on pricing for 7 years in the order form.
- Invoicing: Natalie Chen (finance@synthexlabs.com) is billing contact; we require PO# on invoices and they will process net 30 from invoice date.

If you can push the redline with those items and send a DocuSign link, we can route to our CFO for signature next week.

Best,
